role: independent narrative review; no manuscript files edited
recommended_title: Fixed-threshold transfer and equal-review ranking in breast ultrasound segmentation quality control
alternate_title: Fixed thresholds and review budgets in breast ultrasound segmentation quality control

abstract.objectives: To distinguish transfer of fixed numerical review thresholds from ranking at a fixed review count for breast ultrasound segmentation quality control.
abstract.methods: Frozen SAM predictions used reference-derived, known-location boxes. Confidence and prompt-disagreement thresholds targeting 20% review in 213 development patients were transferred to 851 internal and 252 external patients. Low quality was reference Dice <0.70. Equal-review ranking and a post hoc eight-budget analysis assessed policy dependence.
abstract.results: Confidence-based detection was 71/93 internally and 10/16 externally: −13.84 percentage points (95% confidence interval −38.85 to 7.45). Review fractions were 20.45% and 13.89%, respectively. Externally, disagreement detected 13/16 low-quality masks at its transferred cutoff versus 10/16 for confidence; at 50 reviews per method, the corresponding counts were 13/16 and 14/16. Across targets from 5% to 50%, neither score consistently detected more low-quality masks.
abstract.conclusions: Fixed-threshold transfer and equal-review ranking answer different deployment questions. Their method comparisons depend on the policy and budget, while external detection remains imprecise with 16 low-quality masks. Reporting detection, review fraction and misses together makes this distinction explicit.

introduction_final_paragraph: We therefore evaluated two deployment questions for segmentation quality control: what happens when a development-calibrated numerical cutoff is transferred unchanged, and how the same scores compare when a fixed number of cases can be reviewed. Using confidence and prompt-disagreement scores on identical predictions from a frozen SAM, we calibrated cutoffs to a 20% development review target in BUS-BRA and applied them to internal BUS-BRA and external BrEaST patients. The prespecified analyses examined detection of low-quality masks, review fraction and paired external detection at the locked cutoffs; equal-review ranking addressed the capacity-constrained question separately. Exploratory analyses then examined how the comparison varied across review budgets and under development and test-sample resampling. The contribution is an empirical evaluation of these distinct operating policies, rather than a new uncertainty algorithm.
discussion_first_paragraph: The choice between preserving a numerical cutoff and preserving a review count changes the question asked of a quality-control score. At the transferred cutoffs calibrated to 20% development review, prompt disagreement detected 13 of 16 low-quality external masks and confidence detected 10; when both received 50 reviews, the corresponding counts were 13 and 14. The complete eight-budget analysis showed no uniformly better score. The 20% result therefore illustrates dependence on the operating policy and budget, rather than a general advantage of either score. A ranking comparison alone does not establish how a fixed cutoff will transfer, and a transferred-cutoff comparison does not isolate performance at equal review capacity.
conclusion: In this known-location breast ultrasound evaluation, transferring development-calibrated numerical cutoffs changed the fraction of cases flagged for review. Method comparisons depended on the operating policy and review budget, with no uniform winner across the complete budget grid. External detection remained imprecise because only 16 masks met the low-quality definition. Joint reporting of detection, review fraction and missed cases, with an explicit statement of whether the cutoff or review count is fixed, provides the practical interpretation of these results.

results_drop_ins.budget: Across development targets of 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 40% and 50%, the external B-minus-A detection difference under transferred cutoffs was positive at the first four targets, negative at 25%, 30% and 50%, and zero at 40%. Under equal-review ranking, it was positive at 5%, 10% and 15%, negative at 20%, and zero at the remaining targets. Thus, neither score consistently detected more low-quality masks, and the direction change between policies at 20% was budget-dependent.
results_drop_ins.bootstrap: Three patient-bootstrap routes, each with 10,000 replicates, separately examined test-sample variation at fixed cutoffs, development-calibration variation with the test cohorts unchanged, and both sources together. Under joint development-and-test resampling, the original strict direction pattern, external B-minus-A detection >0 at transferred cutoffs and <0 at 50 reviews, occurred in 3,094/10,000 jointly valid replicates (30.94%); at least one contrast was zero in 28.08%. These are empirical resampling frequencies, not p-values or probabilities that either direction holds in the population. The original Newcombe intervals were retained.
results_drop_ins.case_mix: At the locked cutoffs, the external-minus-internal difference in A's review fraction was −6.56 percentage points. Symmetric Kitagawa accounting across dataset-reported benign/malignant strata gave a +0.64-point composition-associated term and a −7.20-point within-stratum-rate term. The latter also equalled the difference after direct standardization to common diagnostic weights. These terms describe the observed mixture of rates and stratum shares; they do not attribute the difference causally to diagnostic classification.
results_drop_ins.replay: Targeted CPU replay of the six external low-quality cases missed by A generated 30 prediction masks using the byte-identical SAM checkpoint and archived prompt rules. All quality labels and A/B review flags matched the archived records. The maximum absolute difference in initial reference Dice was 9.61 × 10−5. The replay contours provide spatial context for these six cases; all cohort analyses continue to use the original archived scores.

empirical_support_note: At the original fixed cutoffs, the external low-quality sample contained 10 detections by both scores, zero by A alone, three by B alone and three by neither. An empirical bootstrap at those fixed cutoffs cannot generate an unobserved A-only outcome, constraining its B-minus-A contrast to be nonnegative. Its percentile interval of [0.00, 40.00] percentage points therefore does not exclude an A advantage in the population. The original paired Newcombe interval [−4.28, 40.04] percentage points remains the interval for H3.

supplemental_wording.bootstrap_methods: Resample patients independently within development, internal and external cohorts while keeping A, B and quality labels paired; retain repeated draws and rerank the external resample to select exactly 50 draw records when that policy is evaluated. Route 1 fixes the original cutoffs and resamples the test cohorts; route 2 resamples development and recalibrates while retaining the original test cohorts and top-50 rankings; route 3 combines both. Report 10,000 iterations per route, joint-valid denominators and zero contrasts separately.
supplemental_wording.case_mix_methods: For detection, diagnostic weights are F_s/F, the benign/malignant shares among low-quality masks; for review fraction they are N_s/N among all patients. Report the symmetric Kitagawa identity D=C+R and the direct-standardization identity. The separate decomposition bootstrap has 5,000 repetitions, not 10,000; detection components have 4,999 valid draws because one external benign low-quality stratum denominator was zero, while overall detection contrasts have 5,000.
supplemental_wording.replay_caption: Targeted CPU replay of all six external low-quality cases missed by A. Green contours show the released reference and orange contours the newly generated initial prediction; boxes are reference-derived. The first three cases were missed by both scores and the other three were detected by B. All quality and review flags matched the archived results. The original CUDA masks were not archived, so cross-environment pixel identity could not be checked; the maximum absolute initial-reference-Dice difference was 9.61 × 10−5.
supplemental_wording.replay_precision: The 9.61 × 10−5 figure concerns initial reference Dice only. Across all 48 numerical comparisons, the maximum absolute difference was 0.0014354348103 (case105, left-shift consistency Dice). Do not describe every score as agreeing to 10−4 or exactly reproducing. Thirty nonempty newly generated masks were saved; these are six existing patients, not 30 patients or newly independent observations.
supplemental_wording.main_figure_5_caption: Three external low-quality masks missed by both review scores. Green contours show the released reference, orange contours show the initial prediction generated in the targeted CPU replay, and blue boxes show the reference-derived initial prompts. Panel values are the archived scores used for cohort analyses. The newly generated masks provide spatial context; their quality labels and review flags matched the archive. Six-case numerical comparisons and complete replay contours are reported in the supplement.

reviewer_response_templates.text: We have made the operating policy the organizing question of the manuscript. Transferring a development-calibrated numerical cutoff evaluates operating-point transfer; selecting the same number of high-risk cases evaluates ranking at fixed review capacity. We now report all eight target budgets, which show no uniformly better score and prevent the 20% direction change from being presented as a general method advantage. The study's contribution is this empirical distinction, not a new uncertainty algorithm.

We added three patient-bootstrap routes, with 10,000 replicates each, to separate development-calibration variation from test-sample variation. The original strict direction pattern occurred in 30.94% of jointly valid full-resampling replicates. We describe this as an empirical stability frequency and preserve the original Newcombe intervals; it is not a p-value or a population probability. The fixed-cutoff bootstrap's empirical-support boundary is explained alongside its results.

We generated and saved actual prediction masks in a targeted CPU replay of the six audited cases using the byte-identical checkpoint and original prompt rules. All quality labels and A/B flags matched. Initial reference Dice differed by at most 9.61 × 10−5. We now provide the contours with the environment and numerical differences disclosed, retain the original scores for all cohort analyses, and do not claim pixel identity with unarchived CUDA masks.

We added descriptive two-stratum standardization and symmetric Kitagawa accounting using dataset-reported benign/malignant classifications. For A's review fraction, the observed −6.56-point difference comprises +0.64 composition-associated and −7.20 within-stratum-rate points. We describe these as algebraic accounting terms, without attributing causation or claiming that acquisition and annotation differences have been controlled.

avoid: Do not write: B is superior at fixed thresholds; A is the better ranking method. Use observed counts and policy/budget dependence.
Do not call 30.94% a p-value, posterior probability, replication probability, or probability of a population reversal.
Do not call route 2's 90.40% frequency stronger general evidence; the original test patients and rankings are unchanged.
Do not substitute bootstrap percentile intervals for the original prespecified Newcombe intervals.
Do not report a percent explained by diagnosis or say that adjustment removed case mix/confounding.
Do not say exact six-case numerical reproduction or bitwise/pixel-identical predictions; all flags match despite small numerical differences.
Do not merge the older all-1,316 same-environment zero-difference rerun with the new six-case cross-environment CPU replay.
Do not infer clinical review-time savings, inference speed ratios, new patients, independent validation, or independent human-prompt validation.
source_caution: The cloud validation overview and independent resource review predate the completed CPU replay and still describe missing weights or unexecuted replay. Use the later six_case_replay report for current replay status; preserve the earlier reports as historical provenance.
